metadata.title: War Correspondent Philosophy: Method, Evidence, and the Ethics of Research Under a Closing Window
metadata.description:
A 6-volume philosophical treatise on research epistemology, testimonial evidence under adversarial conditions, adversarial falsification governance, temporal corpus evidentialism, human-machine epistemic division of labor, mechanism transfer across non-isomorphic domains, and prospective framework self-revision.

Authored by Gia Bao Huynh (Jun Huynh), Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

metadata.title: The Embedded Witness: Temporal Proximity, Designed Absence, and the Self-Demonstrating Text (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. I)
metadata.description: Volume I of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Investigates temporal proximity to epistemic events, designed absence of retrospective bias, testimonial epistemology under closing windows, and the construction of self-demonstrating documentary texts.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

part_of.title: War Correspondent Philosophy: Method, Evidence, and the Ethics of Research Under a Closing Window

metadata.title: Falsification and Epistemic Self-Governance: Popper, Independent Attack Surfaces, and Catching One's Own Self-Sealing Drift (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. II)
metadata.description: Volume II of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Explores Popperian demarcation, independent adversarial attack surfaces, internal governance protocols, and systematic heuristics for diagnosing and arresting self-sealing epistemic drift.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

metadata.title: Corpus Temporalism: Timestamp as Argument, and Why Sequence Carries Evidential Weight (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. III)
metadata.description: Volume III of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Formulates Corpus Temporalism: the epistemic thesis that cryptographic timestamps and unalterable sequential order carry inherent evidential weight, distinguishing genuine prospective prediction from retrospective accommodation.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

metadata.title: Human–AI Epistemology: Statelessness, Machine-Speed Division of Labor, and the Mechanical Condition (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. IV)
metadata.description: Volume IV of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Analyzes human-machine cognitive collaboration, model statelessness, machine-speed epistemic division of labor, prompt-bound working memory, and the mechanical condition of synthetic intellects.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

metadata.title: Mechanism Transfer and Domain Portability: When a Formal Structure Survives Its Crossing Into a New Domain (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. V)
metadata.description: Volume V of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Examines the epistemology of mechanism transfer: conditions under which formal mathematical and logical structures maintain explanatory validity and empirical power when ported into novel domains.

creators.name: Huynh, Gia Bao
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

metadata.title: The Prospective and Self-Revising Life of a Framework: What a Theory Does After It Is Falsified (War Correspondent Philosophy, Vol. VI)
metadata.description: Volume VI of the War Correspondent Philosophy monograph. Investigates post-falsification dynamics, Lakatosian progressive problem-shifts versus degenerative defense maneuvers, and the ethical responsibility of self-revising theoretical frameworks.
